questions.q: Which is more acidic: acetic acid (CH₃COOH) or ethanol (CH₃CH₂OH)?
c: Acetic acid, because its conjugate base is resonance-stabilized
Ethanol, because it has an O–H bond
Ethanol, because its conjugate base is more basic
questions.e: Acetate delocalizes the negative charge over two oxygens (pKa ≈ 4.8 vs ≈ 16).

questions.q: Which is the stronger base?
questions.e: The conjugate acid with the highest pKa (methanol ≈ 15.5) gives the strongest base.

questions.q: Will sodium amide (NaNH₂) quantitatively deprotonate a terminal alkyne (pKa ≈ 25)? Why?
c: Yes; NH₃ (pKa ≈ 38) is a much weaker acid, so the equilibrium favors the acetylide
No; NH₂⁻ is too weak a base
questions.e: Equilibrium lies on the side of the weaker acid and weaker base; ΔpKa ≈ 13.

questions.q: List the four factors (ARIO) that determine relative acidity of an H–A bond and give a one-line example of each.
questions.m: Atom (electronegativity/size of A: HI > HF in size effect; H–F > H–CH₃ across a period), Resonance (carboxylic acids > alcohols), Induction (CF₃COOH stronger than CH₃COOH), Orbital (sp C–H of alkynes more acidic than sp² and sp³ because of greater s-character).

questions.q: What is the stereochemical outcome of an SN2 reaction at a stereocenter?
c: No change in R/S label always
questions.e: Backside attack inverts the stereocenter (Walden inversion).

questions.q: Which alkyl bromide reacts fastest in an SN2 reaction?
questions.e: Steric hindrance slows backside attack: methyl > primary > secondary >> tertiary.

questions.q: Which solvent best promotes SN2 reactions with an anionic nucleophile?
questions.e: Polar aprotic solvents do not H-bond to the anion, leaving the nucleophile reactive.

questions.q: What geometric requirement applies to a concerted E2 elimination?
c: The β-hydrogen and leaving group should be anti-periplanar
The β-hydrogen and leaving group should be syn-clinal (gauche)
questions.e: Anti-periplanar alignment gives best orbital overlap in the transition state.

questions.q: 2-Bromo-2-methylbutane is treated with NaOEt in EtOH (heat), and in a separate experiment with KOt-Bu in t-BuOH. Predict the major alkene in each and explain.
questions.m: With NaOEt (small, strong base) E2 gives the more substituted Zaitsev product, 2-methylbut-2-ene. With bulky KOt-Bu, steric hindrance favors removal of the more accessible hydrogen from the methyl or CH₂ position to give the Hofmann product, 2-methylbut-1-ene, as the major alkene.

questions.q: The major product of HBr addition to propene (no peroxides) is:
questions.e: Markovnikov: proton adds to give the more stable secondary carbocation.

questions.q: Hydroboration–oxidation (BH₃·THF; then H₂O₂/NaOH) of 1-methylcyclohexene gives mainly:
questions.e: Anti-Markovnikov, syn addition of H and OH across the alkene: OH ends up on C2 trans to the C1 methyl.

questions.q: Which reagent converts an internal alkyne into a cis-alkene?
questions.e: Poisoned Pd gives syn hydrogenation and stops at the alkene; Na/NH₃ gives trans.

questions.q: Treating 3-methyl-1-butene with HBr gives mostly 2-bromo-2-methylbutane. Explain.
questions.m: Protonation at C1 gives a secondary carbocation at C2. A 1,2-hydride shift from the adjacent tertiary C–H converts it into the more stable tertiary carbocation, which is then captured by bromide to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane.

questions.q: NaBH₄ in methanol will reduce a ketone to:
questions.e: Hydride adds to C=O; NaBH₄ normally does not reduce esters or amides.

questions.q: Excess CH₃MgBr reacts with ethyl benzoate; after acidic workup the product is:
questions.e: The ketone intermediate is more reactive than the ester, so two equivalents add, giving a tertiary alcohol with two identical methyl groups.

questions.q: Which carboxylic acid derivative is most reactive toward nucleophilic acyl substitution?
questions.e: Reactivity follows leaving group ability and resonance donation: acid chloride > anhydride > ester ≈ acid > amide.

questions.q: Outline the mechanistic steps of the acid-catalyzed Fischer esterification of a carboxylic acid with an alcohol.
questions.m: Protonate the carbonyl oxygen; alcohol attacks the activated carbonyl carbon; deprotonate to form a tetrahedral intermediate; protonate one OH to make a good leaving group (water); eliminate water to re-form the C=O (protonated ester); deprotonate to give the ester. All steps are reversible (PADPED).

questions.q: Compared with chlorination, free-radical bromination of an alkane is:
c: More selective for the most substituted C–H
questions.e: Br• abstraction is endothermic with a late transition state, so it strongly discriminates between 3°, 2° and 1° hydrogens.

questions.q: Which is a termination step in a radical chain halogenation?
questions.e: Termination consumes two radicals to form a stable bond.

questions.q: A full-headed curved arrow in a polar mechanism represents:
questions.e: Single-electron movement is shown with fishhook (half-headed) arrows.

questions.q: Curved arrows for a nucleophilic attack should start at ____ and end at ____.
c: the nucleophile's lone pair or bond; the electrophilic atom
questions.e: Arrows always show electron flow from electron-rich to electron-poor sites.
